'''Christopher Steven Stigall''' (born January 5, 1977) is an American politician, conservative<ref name=Fiorillo-Out/> talk radio personality, cable news contributor,  online columnist and host of The Chris Stigall podcast. He currently hosts the morning show on [[Salem Media Group]]'s AM 990 The Answer in [[Philadelphia]], and was the prior host of [[WPHT]] Morning Show in the [[Delaware Valley]] market from 2011 to March 2019.  Previously, he hosted The [[KCMO (AM)]] Morning Show in the [[Kansas City Metropolitan Area|Kansas City]] market from 2006 until 2010.

Stigall launched a nationally-syndicated show on the [[Salem Radio Network]] in January 2025, hosting the morning show from 6 to 9 AM [[Eastern Time Zone|EST]]. He replaced [[Hugh Hewitt]], whose show moved to the 3 to 6 PM slot in order to replace [[Sebastian Gorka]], who left Salem to join the [[Second presidency of Donald Trump|second Trump administration]].<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20241206697004/en/Salem-Radio-Network-and-Salem-News-Channel-Announce-Lineup-Changes|work=[[Business Wire]]|date=December 9, 2024|title=Salem Radio Network and Salem News Channel Announce Lineup Changes}}</ref>

Stigall was the Republican nominee for [[Missouri's 6th congressional district]] in [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Missouri#District 6|2026]], where he won.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.kansascity.com/news/politics-government/article316717076.html|title=Radio host Chris Stigall wins GOP primary for Rep. Sam Graves' Northland seat|first=Kacen|last=Bayless|date=August 5, 2026|access-date=August 5, 2026|work=[[Kansas City Star]]}}</ref> He gave up his nationally-syndicated talk show to seek public service in the U.S. House of Representatives, as have others from the Salem Radio Network.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tradup |first=Tom |date=2026-08-08 |title=Salem Radio Network: Petri Dish for National Politics |url=https://townhall.com/columnists/tomtradup/2026/08/08/salem-radio-network-petri-dish-for-national-politics-n2680909 |access-date=2026-08-10 |website=townhall.com |language=en}}</ref> 

==Education and early career==

Stigall graduated from [[Northwest Missouri State University]], where he studied comedy writing and television production as an intern with the ''[[Late Show with David Letterman]]'' in New York. Stigall also served as a representative and press assistant to U.S. Representative [[Sam Graves]], and later went on to work in Kansas City radio in 1999.

==Career==

In 2009, Stigall was selected as the master of ceremonies at the Mayor's Christmas Tree lighting ceremony.<ref>{{cite news|last=Hendricks|first=Mike|title=Ulterior motives lurk behind the tree-lighting ceremony|url=http://www.kansascity.com/2009/11/19/1581990/ulterior-motives-lurk-behind-the.html|accessdate=July 23, 2010|newspaper=Kansas City Star|date=November 19, 2009}}</ref>

On November 18, 2010, WPHT in Philadelphia announced that Stigall will be anchoring its morning show focused on "local and national policy, the economy, the biggest news stories and issues that affect all Philadelphians, coupled with interviews of the day's news and decision makers."<ref>{{cite news|title=WPHT To Launch New Lineup With Chris Stigall Hosting Morning Drive|url=https://philadelphia.cbslocal.com/2010/11/18/wpht-to-launch-new-lineup-with-chris-stigall-hosting-morning-drive-beginning-january-3-2011/|accessdate=November 18, 2010|newspaper=CBS Philly|date=November 30, 2010}}</ref>

On March 6, 2019, Stigall and WPHT ended their broadcast partnership after 8-plus years, according to insiders the "split wasn't unpleasant."<ref name=Fiorillo-Out>{{cite magazine|last=Fiorillo|first=Victor|title=Conservative Radio Host Chris Stigall Out at 1210AM|url=https://www.phillymag.com/news/2019/03/06/chris-stigall-1210am|accessdate=March 6, 2019|magazine=[[Philadelphia (magazine)|Philadelphia]]|date=March 6, 2019}}</ref> Stigall went on to launch a podcast version of his previous radio show featuring his former co-host Paige Powers.<ref>{{cite magazine|last=Fiorillo|first=Victor|title=What Happened to Chris Stigall After He Left 1210AM? A Podcast, of Course|url=https://www.phillymag.com/news/2019/05/15/chris-stigall-podcast|magazine=[[Philadelphia (magazine)|Philadelphia]]|date=May 15, 2019}}</ref>

Stigall has filled in for nationally-syndicated hosts [[Michael Savage (commentator)|Michael Savage]], [[Rusty Humphries]], [[Lou Dobbs]], [[Fred Thompson]], [[Jerry Doyle (radio host)|Jerry Doyle]], [[Steve Malzberg]], and Sebastian Gorka.  He has also been a contributor for Salem-owned outlets ''[[Townhall]]'' and ''[[Human Events]]'', as well as [[Andrew Breitbart]]'s ''BigHollywood'', ''[[Philadelphia (magazine)|Philadelphia]]'', ''[[The American Spectator]]'', and the ''Platte County Landmark''.

==Sharyl Attkisson revelation==
On May 25, 2013, Stigall conducted an interview with [[Sharyl Attkisson]] and inquired about if she suspected her computer of being hacked as a part of the [[2013 Department of Justice investigations of reporters]]. Attkisson responded that her personal and work computers had been compromised and were under investigation.<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.politico.com/blogs/media/2013/05/sharyl-attkissons-computers-compromised-164456|work=[[Politico]]|date=May 21, 2013|title=Sharyl Attkisson's Computers Compromised|last1=Byers|first1=Dylan}}</ref> She responded, "I think there could be some relationship between these types of things and what happened to me," adding that "something suspicious had been happening since."<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.huffingtonpost.com/2013/05/21/sharyl-attkisson-computers-compromised-cbs_n_3313199.html|work=[[The Huffington Post]]|date=21 May 2013|title=CBS' Sharyl Attkisson: My Computers Were Compromised, 'Could Be Some Relationship' To DOJ Scandals|last1=Mirkinson|first1=Jack}}</ref> Stigall then had a media clash with [[Erik Wemple]] from ''[[The Washington Post]]''. Prior to the release of Attkisson's book, Wemple had criticized her for "ladling out hints and half-assertions about the violations of her computers, as she was apparently holding back details that could assist the public in determining just who was responsible for them."<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/erik-wemple/wp/2014/10/29/philadelphia-radio-host-hammers-erik-wemple-blog-to-smithereens-over-sharyl-attkisson/|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]|date=October 29, 2014|title=Philadelphia Radio Host Hammers Erik Wemple Blog to Smithereens Over Sharyl Attkisson|last1=Wemple|first1=Erik}}</ref> Her 2014 book ''Stonewalled'' chronicled her on-air exchange with Stigall and revealed that it was an unexpected encounter for her that became a national news story.

==Political career==
===2026 Congressional campaign===
{{see|2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Missouri#District 6}}
On March 27, 2026, Stigall joined five Republicans running to replace retiring U.S. Representative [[Sam Graves]] in [[Missouri's 6th congressional district]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cunningham |first=Joe |date=2026-03-27 |title=National Conservative Radio Host Leaves the Microphone Behind to Run for Congress |url=https://redstate.com/joesquire/2026/03/27/national-conservative-radio-host-leaves-the-microphone-behind-to-run-for-congress-n2200707 |access-date=2026-07-21 |website=redstate.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Jahraus |first=Seth |title=Why Chris Stigall is running for Missouri's 6th District |url=https://www.kcur.org/podcast/kansas-city-today/2026-07-21/conservative-radio-host-chris-stigall-missouris-6th-district |access-date=2026-07-21 |website=KCUR - Kansas City news and NPR |language=en}}</ref>

Endorsed in the race by Graves,<ref>{{Cite news |last=Bayless |first=Kacen |date=2026-07-26 |title=Inside the heated race to represent Kansas City’s Northland in Congress |url=https://www.kansascity.com/news/politics-government/article316643158.html |access-date=2026-07-27 |work=The Kansas City Star}}</ref> he won the five-way Republican primary on August 4, 2026 with 44% of the vote, beating second-place finisher, Kansas City Council member Nathan Willett, by 12 percentage points.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Quinn |first=Steph |last2=Hanshaw |first2=Annelise |date=2026-08-05 |title=Chris Stigall wins Republican primary for Missouri’s 6th Congressional District |url=https://missouriindependent.com/2026/08/04/chris-stigall-wins-republican-primary-for-missouris-6th-congressional-district/ |access-date=2026-08-05 |website=Missouri Independent |language=en-US}}</ref> Stigall outlines his plans for winning the general election in November thusly:<ref>{{Cite web |last=City |first=Josephfer Williams Kansas |title=Chris Stigall sits down for a Q&A ahead of 2026 Midterm Election |url=https://spectrumlocalnews.com/nys/buffalo/news/2026/08/20/chris-stigall-sits-down-for-a-q-a-ahead-of-2026-midterm-election |access-date=2026-08-21 |website=spectrumlocalnews.com |language=en}}</ref>

{{Blockquote|text=The 6th District is a huge, huge district with 33 counties. Our biggest task as we close out this race heading into November is to get to as many of those counties as often as possible. We need to meet folks where they are and hear the various concerns that they have. It's a lot of rural counties that all have very unique needs. Many are similar, but with a lot of land to cover, with a lot of people to represent.}}Stigall strongly supports reducing Federal government spending, saying this must be a priority for Congress. "I wouldn't mind seeing a balanced budget amendment," he says.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pournazari |first=Skye |date=2026-10-16 |title=Stigall outlines health care, agriculture and economic priorities in 6th District race |url=https://www.newspressnow.com/news/local_news/government/stigall-outlines-health-care-agriculture-and-economic-priorities-in-6th-district-race/article_9ba82678-d388-4953-879b-7ebf1c505049.html |access-date=2026-10-16 |website=News-Press NOW |language=en}}</ref> On the military actions in Iran, Stigall says: "So doing the right thing and leading is a very difficult thing to do. But this is a 50-year plague, not just in that region, but to the world that the president decided to deal with despite the politics of it."<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-10-28 |title=Meet the Candidates: Chris Stigall |url=https://www.kmaland.com/news/meet-the-candidates-chris-stigall/article_2c086b60-58e5-4412-8835-b658cb751776.html |access-date=2026-10-30 |website=KMAland.com |language=en}}</ref>

Stigall beat his Democrat opponent, Josh Smead, 58% to 39% (as of 10:30 pm) to take the seat.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mansouri |first=Kavahn |date=2026-11-04 |title=Republican Chris Stigall wins Missouri's open 6th District seat |url=https://www.kcur.org/politics-elections-and-government/2026-11-03/republican-chris-stigall-wins-open-6th-district-seat |access-date=2026-11-04 |website=KCUR - Kansas City news and NPR |language=en}}</ref>

==Charity work==
Through a partnership with the Pennsylvania SPCA and the Piazza Auto Group, Stigall has helped find homes for over 100 shelter animals through his weekly on-air segment "The Piazza Pet of the Week."<ref>{{citation|url=http://philadelphia.cbslocal.com/piazzapet/|work=[[CBS Philadelphia]]|title=Piazza Pet of the Week}}</ref>

Philadelphia's USO chapter known as Liberty USO has partnered with Stigall and the Philadelphia Phillies to surprise military service members annually with a trip to Phillies Fantasy Camp in [[Clearwater, Florida]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.philliesphantasycamp.com/blog/2014/01/wounded-warrior-joins-the-phantasy-camp-team/|date=January 8, 2014|title=Wounded Warrior Joins the Phantasy Camp}}</ref>

==Controversy==
In March 2011, Stigall became heavily involved in the Delaware County priest trial. Stigall thought ''[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]'' was heavily biased in its coverage and one priest and his lawyer declared their innocence on Stigall's morning talk show.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://articles.philly.com/2011-03-15/news/28691697_1_priest-accuser-radio-show|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120426182754/http://articles.philly.com/2011-03-15/news/28691697_1_priest-accuser-radio-show|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 26, 2012|work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]] | date=March 15, 2011|title=Priest declares innocence, lawyer rips judge on radio show|last1=Mucha|first1=Peter}}</ref>
